# USR-003: Cloud default account is locked down

- **Group:** Users and privilege
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

Cloud images create a well known first account (ubuntu, debian, admin, ec2-user), often with passwordless sudo and the provisioning key. Once you have your own admin account, the default one is a known username for attackers to target and a spare way in nobody reviews.

## Verify by hand

```sh
getent passwd ubuntu debian admin ec2-user; sudo grep -r NOPASSWD /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d
```

## How to fix it

Lock it: `passwd -l <user>`, set its shell to nologin, move its authorized_keys aside and drop its NOPASSWD line. Keep your own admin account working first.

## What a fix can break

If the default account is also what your provider console or automation logs in with, locking it removes that path.

Run `stackward explain USR-003` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
